description.narrative: Community seed banks safeguard genetic diversity of local crops including NUS and increase utilization by the community for food and nutrition security in the face of climate change. Over the past years, CTDT Zambia has been working with rural communities on measures to enhance genetic diversity and reverse the rapid genetic erosion that has led to a reduction of available varieties necessaryto achieve household food and nutrition security while having to deal with the threat of climate change. This work has involved measures to restore some of the lost farmer varieties and to introduce new ones and make improvements to them and to existing ones. This increase in diversity has been necessitated by the threat ofclimate change where inadequate diversity has led to reduced capacity to adapt, leading to reduced harvests due to drought and inconsistent rainfall patterns. This work has involved community multiplication of diverse varieties of diverse crops to increase seed availability in the target communities. In order to have a viable, perpetual and sustainable system of community seed multiplication and distribution, communities agreed to utilize volunteer household spaces as temporary community seed banks, where incoming seed due for multiplication could be stored and where harvested seed was re-distributed from. Over the years, the increasing number of crops and varieties has caused an increase in the quantities of seed and samples passing through the seed bank with some of them requiring to be kept longer than one season. This has necessitated increased management attention to deal with effects of pests and diseases and the storage environment in general. Thus, community seed bank committees have been established to manage the systems and to lead the development of rules and guidelines for seed bank operations. These communities are now ready to have permanent purpose-built structures for use as community seed banks and centres for sharing knowledge around issues of seed in their communities. With this project it is planned to construct one community seed bank with the active participation of community members and their contribution to the cost of construction through utilization of locally produced bricks and use of local artisan skills and bricklaying. It is planned that the community seed bank will form the centre around which all the activities around seed in the community will revolve including farmer field schools and adequateland for purposes of establishing demonstration plots for farmer learnings. Adequate land will also be reserved for characterization of the germplasm in the seedbank and for crop development and seed multiplication Oxfam Novib will support this project through monitoring progress, finance management, providing advice and reporting to the donor.

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib was founded in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Oxfam Novib is member of the Oxfam International confederation. Working together in the confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education for all, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam Novib's main office is based in The Netherlands, it supports the work of a network of local offices, the implementation of global projects, fundraising, campaigning and advocacy. Oxfam Novib’s the Hague office contributes towards this project’s implementation.
